newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila stocks bounce on property, banks recovery.
newsitem.headline: Manila stocks bounce on property, banks recovery.

text.p: * Foreign and local brokers give mix reviews
Manila stocks broke a seven-day losing streak by ending higher on Thursday as investors bought property and banking issues at year-low levels, traders said.
But some brokers said the worst is not yet over. "It's too early to discount the bears out. It could (today's rise) just be a dead cat's bounce," said ING Baring Securities analyst Louie Bate.
The main index ended at 2,949.02 points, up 39.72.
The main index had lost 9.73 percent since it began sinking on March 31 on fears of a property crash due to a glut. The market paused from the foreign selldown on Wednesday due to a holiday.
Bargain hunting in property and banking issues on Thursday lifted the market across the board.
"We have finally been liberated from our seven-day losing streak. Today is an independence day," said Henry Ong, trader at Sapphire Securities.
Bate said bargain hunters emerged today because "some issues have been unjustly sold out in the past days."
Wilfred Son Keng Po, sales and research head at Angping Securities, said the market picked up volume at midsession.
Some 3.3 billion pesos worth of shares changed hands as gainers outpaced losers 103 to 51.

Son Keng Po said he expected the market to consolidate at the 2,850 to 3,000 level in next few days. "The market will look for direction to reports of the first quarter earnings of companies," he said.

Megaworld Properties and Holdings Inc gained 70 centavos to seven pesos while its mass housing unit Empire East Land Holdings Inc gained 50 centavos to 6.30 pesos. Both issues led the rally of the property sector.
Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co gained 30 pesos to 630 pesos.
